key_idea: Build a directed 'rests on' graph between pieces plus a floor node; with at most two top pieces the cheapest stable set is two shortest paths that merge at some piece and continue together to the floor.
sketch: Add an edge A->B whenever a cell of A is directly above a cell of a different piece B, and A->floor for pieces in the bottom row. BFS from each top piece on the graph and from the floor on the reversed graph; the answer is min over meeting nodes v (including the floor itself, which covers disjoint paths, and v equal to a top piece) of d1[v]+d2[v]+dFloor[v], where edge counts equal piece counts once the floor is excluded. If the top row has a single piece both sources coincide and the formula degenerates to its distance to the floor. O(h*w). Pitfalls: only vertical adjacency gives support (side contact and corner contact do not), and a piece may be supported through a piece nested in its hole.
